thread:
deploy-bot: Started config-only rollout (cfg-2026-03-20-rl1) initiated by alex. Targets: routing.policies, request.timeouts, batching.window, per-customer.rate_limits. Canary=5%. Change window 18:00-19:00 UTC. Release notes: https://redwood.internal/releases/2026-03-20-config

alex: Kicking off. I'm pinning the manifest as cfg-2026-03-20-rl1 for the canary group. Will monitor for 30m.

maya: Watching dashboards — alert thresholds: p99 > 300ms or 5xx > 0.5%.

devin: FYI I changed batching.window 40ms -> 30ms (to reduce tail token latency) and tightened request.timeout 60s -> 45s. No model changes.

sam: Routing tweak: prefer cheap-variant in us-west unless observed latency > 200ms. Added queue-depth backoff policy.

irene: Tests looked good locally. Added fallback to quantized variant for overloads.

deploy-bot: Metric alert: canary nodes (5%) reporting 5xx rate 0.8% over last 5m — above threshold.

maya: Seeing a spike. p50 okay, but p99 up to 410ms on two hosts. Do we want to rollback the canary?

alex: Standby while I check logs. @devin @sam any core dumps or obvious errors?

devin: No core dumps. I'm seeing repeated kvcache OOM in gpu-serve-2 logs around 17:52 UTC. Snippet:
```
E gpu_infer: kvcache_alloc failed: out of memory
```

sam: That matches theory — shrinking batching.window increased concurrency and bumped KV usage. Suggest revert batching.window to 40ms for canary and reevaluate.

alex: Agree. Triggering config rollback on canary only.

deploy-bot: Executing rollback: cfg-2026-03-20-rl1 -> cfg-2026-03-15-stable on canary subset. Rollback initiated by alex.

deploy-bot: Rollback complete on canary at 1739894445. Monitoring metrics.

maya: Post-rollback metrics look good: 5xx down to 0.06%, p99 back to ~220ms. :thumbsup:

alex: Closing the change window early. We'll rework batching strategy before reattempt. Added note to release doc: https://redwood.internal/releases/2026-03-20-config#notes

devin: I'll open a PR with an alternative that reduces concurrent KV allocations instead of shrinking batch window (proposal: serialized KV reserve or staged refill).

irene: Also adding an automated guard: if kvcache OOMs on canary, auto-increase cache or reduce concurrency (runbook PR incoming).

alex: Thanks team. Let's do a short blameless postmortem in eng-releases later today and capture the rollback decision in the release notes.
